# Complete Red-Black Tree Tutorial in C++

7. [Complete Working Code](#7-complete-working-code)
8. [Testing & Verification](#8-testing--verification)

---

## 1. Introduction & Properties

A **Red-Black Tree (RBT)** is a self-balancing Binary Search Tree (BST). It guarantees O(log n) worst-case time for insertion, deletion, and search by enforcing five invariants:

| # | Property |
|---|----------|
| 1 | Every node is either **RED** or **BLACK**. |
| 2 | The **root** is always BLACK. |
| 3 | Every **NIL** (null/leaf) node is BLACK. |
| 4 | A **RED** node cannot have a RED child (no two consecutive reds). |
| 5 | Every path from any node to its descendant NILs contains the **same number of black nodes** (black-height). |

These rules ensure the longest path is at most **twice** the shortest path, keeping the tree height ≤ 2·log₂(n+1).

### Why not AVL?

AVL trees are more strictly balanced (height difference ≤ 1), giving faster lookups. RBTs require **fewer rotations** on insertion/deletion (at most 2 rotations for insert, 3 for delete), making them better for write-heavy workloads. This is why `std::map`, `std::set`, and Linux's CFS scheduler use RBTs.
